summary: Iter_12 backend-only verification of the new Tenant Waitlist module (rental/tenant_leads_router.py) deployed at https://ross-house-backend-production.up.railway.app. Created /app/ross-house-backend/tests/test_tenant_waitlist.py with 18 pytest cases covering the full PUBLIC + ADMIN surface (create/dedup/validation, check, list/filter/stats, PATCH status with invalid-status guard, settings GET/PUT toggle persistence, CSV export, per-lead notify with both channel flags, delete, and unauthenticated-access rejection). 17/18 PASS. ONE REAL BACKEND BUG FOUND: GET /api/admin/tenant-leads/export/csv returns HTTP 500 — root cause is unsafe f-string formatting on a nullable field (monthly_income, defaults to None in the Pydantic model and gets persisted as None). Front-end was NOT tested per user instructions (Next.js code not yet pushed to Vercel; testing agent was told to focus on backend). Local supervised backend at /app/backend/ remains broken (KeyError: MONGO_URL) as documented in the review request — not in scope.

critical.issue: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error. RCA: In tenant_leads_router.py line ~577 the CSV row builder formats `lead.get('monthly_income', 0)` with f-string `f"${...:,.0f}"`. The Pydantic model declares `monthly_income: Optional[float] = None`, so when a lead has no income provided, the stored value is literally `None` (not absent). `dict.get('monthly_income', 0)` returns `None` (key present), and `f"${None:,.0f}"` raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__`. Same latent risk also exists for `max_budget` (line 572) and any other nullable numeric column. Reproduced cleanly against Railway prod after creating a QA lead with no monthly_income.

minor.issue: Returned 200 with email_sent=false, sms_sent=false in test env (no SendGrid/Twilio creds bound) — endpoint behaviour is correct (boolean response, no crash), but no negative path test exists for what happens if the lead's email is malformed or Twilio rate-limits. Consider explicit logging of provider error codes.

action_items: FIX CRITICAL: In /app/ross-house-backend/rental/tenant_leads_router.py admin_export_csv(), guard nullable numeric fields before formatting. Suggested patch — replace `f"${lead.get('monthly_income', 0):,.0f}"` with `f"${(lead.get('monthly_income') or 0):,.0f}"` (and the same for `max_budget` on the previous line). Even better, write a small helper `_money(v)` that returns 'N/A' when value is None.
Add a regression unit test that calls admin_export_csv() with a lead whose monthly_income=None and asserts 200 + content-type text/csv.
After fix is deployed on Railway, re-run /app/ross-house-backend/tests/test_tenant_waitlist.py — should be 18/18.

Frontend (Next.js /interesados, /interesados/en, WaitlistBanner, /admin/interesados): not deployed yet — user must press 'Save to GitHub' first. Once deployed, re-trigger this testing agent with focus on frontend.
Optional defense-in-depth: in CSV row builder, also CSV-escape values that contain literal double quotes (`replace('"', '""')`) — currently only newlines in admin_notes are sanitized.
critical_code_review_comments: tenant_leads_router.py is 609 lines — within the 700-line guideline but approaching it. Two responsibilities (CRUD + notifications) are well separated by helpers, no immediate need to split.

Email validation uses a hand-rolled regex via @validator + the field is typed `str` instead of `EmailStr`. The dependency on `pydantic.EmailStr` is imported but unused. Recommend switching `email: str` → `email: EmailStr` for stricter validation (and align with Pydantic v2 behaviour).

Default dedup logic on POST /public/tenant-leads always updates the existing record's name/phone/etc. from the new payload but preserves the original `created_at`, `status`, `admin_notes`. This means a returning user can change e.g. their phone — good. But it also means a spammer can mutate a real lead's data by posting with the same email. Consider adding a basic rate-limit or anti-spam check (e.g., reCAPTCHA), or skip overwriting if existing.status != 'new'.

_send_welcome / _notify_admin_new_lead are awaited inline inside the public POST handler. If SendGrid is slow, the user's form submit will block on it. Consider FastAPI BackgroundTasks or asyncio.create_task() for fire-and-forget delivery.
auth_admin() in shared.py logs no audit trail — recommended to log admin user + endpoint on every admin call for compliance.

VALID_STATUSES is defined as a module-level list; the Pydantic TenantLeadUpdate model does not use a Literal/Enum to validate status at parse time — the validation is done manually inside admin_update_lead. Tighter to use `status: Optional[Literal['new','contacted',...]]`.

Route /admin/tenant-leads/{lead_id} (line 379) is declared BEFORE /admin/tenant-leads/match/{property_id} (line 545), /admin/tenant-leads/export/csv (line 558), and /admin/tenant-leads/stats (line 361) is ABOVE. FastAPI honours declaration order: stats works, but `/match/{property_id}` could be matched by `/{lead_id}` first if the {lead_id} pattern were registered before. Currently safe because stats and match have unique sub-paths or are above {lead_id}, but the {lead_id}/notify endpoint at line 422 is BELOW {lead_id} — fine. However, `/admin/tenant-leads/notify-property` (line 457) is BELOW `/{lead_id}` — FastAPI would try to match `notify-property` as a lead_id. Recommend reordering: declare all literal/static sub-paths (stats, match/{...}, export/csv, notify-property) BEFORE the catch-all `/{lead_id}` route to avoid future surprises.

rca_of_issue:
BUG: GET /api/admin/tenant-leads/export/csv returns HTTP 500.

Reproduction:
1. POST /api/public/tenant-leads with payload {name, email, phone, bedrooms_wanted, max_budget, language_pref} — omit `monthly_income` (it is Optional in TenantLeadCreate).
2. POST /api/public/marketplace-login with admin creds → grab `token`.
3. GET /api/admin/tenant-leads/export/csv with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` → HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

Root cause (line 577 of /app/ross-house-backend/rental/tenant_leads_router.py):
    rows.append([..., f"${lead.get('monthly_income', 0):,.0f}", ...])
When the lead document has `monthly_income: None` (which is the default the Pydantic model writes), `dict.get('monthly_income', 0)` returns None (because the key IS present, just with a None value — `.get(key, default)` only returns the default when the key is ABSENT). Then `f"${None:,.0f}"` raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__`. The exception bubbles up to FastAPI which returns 500.

The identical pattern exists on the previous line for `max_budget` — currently safe because max_budget is required (no None possible from the API path), but a manual DB edit or future schema change could trigger the same crash.

Mitigation (one-line patch):
    # Before
    f"${lead.get('monthly_income', 0):,.0f}"
    # After
    f"${(lead.get('monthly_income') or 0):,.0f}"

The `or 0` idiom collapses both `None` and missing-key cases to 0. Apply the same pattern to `max_budget` for defense in depth. Add a unit test that calls the endpoint after inserting a lead with monthly_income=None to prevent regression.
